output.brief: The fall in first-contact resolution was most likely caused by Finance's 14 April change, not the new starters. It cut the amount an agent can credit on a call from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments are now blocked and sent automatically to the back-office Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in the same week FCR fell. Referred calls resolve first time only about 34% of the time, and non-referred calls about 82%, both unchanged. The drop is the same for April starters, 6–24 month agents and 24+ month agents, so inexperience doesn't explain it. Tariff enquiries are a small share and resolve as well as before. Overall FCR fell from 75% to 67% while the other changes show no matching signature, though I haven't tested the IVR change or workload directly. Do not put April starters on performance plans: the evidence says it would punish the wrong people. Next step: agree a revised in-call credit limit with Finance, backed by post-call sampling of credits, and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Track FCR and the unsupported-credit rate before any wider rollout. Also have MI add referral status to regular reporting; that can be done much more cheaply than a full dashboard rebuild. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis.
